[Source coding](source-coding.qmd) shows that the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) of a source is the least average length of a code for it,
up to one [bit](entropy.qmd#def-bit).
This page asks which codes a decoder can read one codeword at a time,
and how long such a code must be.

## Optimality {#sec-huffman-optimality}

<!-- No slidebreak here: the heading shares its slide with the thm-huffman-optimal div. -->

{{< include ids/_subfiles/_thm-huffman-optimal.qmd >}}

A [Huffman code](#def-huffman-code) also stays within one [bit](entropy.qmd#def-bit) of the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy).
By the [source coding theorem](source-coding.qmd#thm-source-coding),
every [prefix code](#def-prefix-code) has $L \ge \entropyf{X}$.
Giving each value $x$ the length $\lceil -\log_2 p(x) \rceil$
satisfies the sum in @thm-kraft-inequality,
because $2^{-\lceil -\log_2 p(x) \rceil} \le p(x)$ adds up to at most $1$,
so @thm-kraft-converse gives a prefix code with these lengths,
whose [expected length](source-coding.qmd#def-expected-length) is below $\entropyf{X} + 1$.
By @thm-huffman-optimal,
a Huffman code is at least as short, so
$\entropyf{X} \le L < \entropyf{X} + 1$.
